column3: NASB follows the critical text, rendering the verb as “concluded it was Alexander”; the meaning is uncertain.
NASB follows the critical text; “one cry” is rendered “a single outcry.”
NASB follows the critical text without “goddess”; “temple-keeper” is rendered “guardian of the temple,” and it supplies “the image.”
NASB follows the critical text (“our goddess”); it adds “here.”
NASB renders “courts are conducted” as “the courts are in session” and adds “available.”
NASB follows the critical text; “inquire” is rendered “want.”
NASB follows the critical text; “insurrection” is rendered “riot,” and “commotion” is “disorderly gathering.” It restructures the verse. A stray quotation mark appears in the NASB text.
